answer: Here is one mechanism that works: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because vertex only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, ripple is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any basalt approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
